title: Prosciutto di San Daniele con Fichi
localName: Prosciutto di San Daniele con Fichi
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Delicate, sweet San Daniele prosciutto, prized for its notably mellow, less salty character, draped simply over ripe fresh figs for a striking autumn antipasto.
longDesc: Prosciutto di San Daniele, produced in a small Friulian town under strict protected-origin rules, is generally considered sweeter and less intensely salty than Parma ham, making it a particularly graceful match for ripe, honeyed fresh figs.
ingredients: 150 g (5.3 oz) Prosciutto di San Daniele, thinly sliced
A few fresh basil or mint leaves (optional)
steps: Arrange the halved figs on a serving platter, cut side up.
Drape or wrap each fig half with a slice of San Daniele prosciutto.
Finish with a crack of black pepper and a few torn basil or mint leaves if using.
chefTips: Genuinely ripe, fragrant figs make all the difference in this simple pairing.
San Daniele milder character pairs especially well with fruit compared to saltier prosciutto varieties.
Serve at room temperature rather than chilled, which allows both the ham and figs to show their full flavor.
commonMistakes: Using underripe figs, which lack the sweetness this simple dish depends on entirely.
Over-drizzling with honey, which can overwhelm the delicate balance between the ham and fruit.
Serving straight from the refrigerator, which mutes the flavors of both ingredients.
servedWith: A chilled glass of Prosecco or a light Friulian white wine
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Figs provide fiber and natural sweetness; prosciutto contributes protein.
culturalNote: Prosciutto di San Daniele holds a protected designation of origin, produced exclusively in the small Friulian town it's named for, and is considered one of Italy's two most prestigious cured hams alongside Parma.
